answer: What is the cheapest lie an attacker can tell? Not a fake account, a cheap one, so stop asking whether an identity is real and start asking what it costs in figures: a 16-epoch pending TTL on unanswered rows. Start here: strip the ivory away and the cluster has nothing left to stand on. Someone will object that sparse activity is a tundra, not a proof of honesty, and they are missing the cost model. Then the second constraint, which is the one most designs skip: 1 funder edge collapses a 500-wallet cluster to a single node. Remember that the lotus is cheap to claim and expensive to prove.
